summary: Kyle Larson, a Hendrick Motorsports Cup Series driver, co-owns the High Limit Racing Sprint Car Series with brother-in-law Brad Sweet. At the Commonwealth Clash at Lernerville Speedway, Dale Earnhardt Jr. interviewed them about the series' origins. Larson said he was inspired by FloRacing's Tuesday night late model series and hoped to pressure weekend shows to raise purses. Larson led late but lost control while defending against Sweet and finished eighth, while David Gravel won $50,000.
one_line: Kyle Larson explains to Dale Earnhardt Jr. why he and Brad Sweet launched the High Limit Racing Sprint Car Series, and recounts his eighth-place finish at Lernerville.
key_facts: Kyle Larson is a Hendrick Motorsports driver and a title contender in the NASCAR Cup Series.
Larson co-owns the High Limits Racing Sprint Car Series with brother-in-law Brad Sweet, a four-time World of Outlaws Series champion.
Dale Earnhardt Jr. attended High Limit Racing's Commonwealth Clash at Lernerville Speedway on Tuesday.
Brad Sweet was formerly a development driver for JR Motorsports in the NASCAR Nationwide Series, giving him a working relationship with Earnhardt Jr.
According to Larson, Earnhardt Jr. requested to visit the event and urged Larson to take part in the race.
Larson said he did not want a series based solely around himself and wanted to help other racers.
Larson's inspiration came from racing late models: FloRacing's Tuesday night late model series pays 20 some thousand to win every Tuesday, so he asked why it wouldn't work in sprint cars.
The winner of the Lernerville race, David Gravel, earned $50,000.
Larson hoped the series would pressure weekend shows to raise their purses and said he has seen a big step in that this year.
Larson was leading with nine laps to go at Lernerville but lost control while defending the lead from Brad Sweet.
Unlike in Texas, Larson did not DNF at Lernerville but finished eighth.
Larson is the 2021 Cup Series champion.
Events like these help keep smaller race tracks across the country in good shape.
